title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten under-21-safe, no-admission activities at UC and nearby public cultural and park spaces.

cards.entity_name: Dorothy W. and C. Lawson Reed, Jr. Gallery
cards.title: See a Reed Gallery exhibition
cards.subtitle: DAAP Building, UC Uptown Campus
cards.notes: Enter through DAAP’s third-floor Clifton Court entrance, then take time with the rotating exhibition on the fifth floor.
cards.short_summary: A public DAAP gallery for viewing contemporary and occasional historical exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: UC identifies the Reed Gallery as a DAAP Gallery for the university and regional public; UC materials describe Reed Gallery exhibitions as open free to the public.
cards.source_title: Reed Gallery Past Exhibits | University of Cincinnati
cards.access_notes: Gallery hours listed by UC are Sunday–Thursday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; check the current exhibition before going.

cards.entity_name: Philip M. Meyers, Jr. Memorial Gallery
cards.title: Browse the Meyers Gallery
cards.subtitle: Steger Student Life Center, UC Uptown Campus
cards.notes: Walk UC MainStreet to the Steger Student Life Center and look for the ground-floor gallery across from Nippert Stadium.
cards.short_summary: A UC gallery presenting DAAP faculty, student, and wider university work.
cards.evidence_claim: UC says the Meyers Gallery serves the university community and presents DAAP faculty and student work; UC identifies its galleries as open to everyone.
cards.access_notes: UC lists Sunday–Thursday hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; exhibitions rotate, so confirm availability first.

cards.title: Explore the permanent collection
cards.subtitle: Eden Park
cards.notes: Use free general admission to spend an afternoon with the collection, then continue on the surrounding Eden Park paths.
cards.short_summary: An art-museum visit with no general-admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Cincinnati states that Cincinnati Art Museum general admission and parking are free.
cards.source_title: The ultimate guide to Cincinnati for college students | University of Cincinnati
cards.access_notes: This applies to general admission; confirm any special-exhibition requirements directly with the museum.

cards.title: Take in contemporary art at CAC
cards.subtitle: 44 East Sixth Street, downtown Cincinnati
cards.notes: Make a self-guided lap through the galleries and pause to discuss one work that catches your group’s attention.
cards.short_summary: A downtown contemporary-art stop with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The University of Cincinnati states that admission to the Contemporary Arts Center is free.
cards.source_title: The ultimate guide to Cincinnati for college students | University of Cincinnati
cards.access_notes: Check the center’s current visitor information for gallery availability and program-specific details.

cards.entity_name: William Howard Taft National Historic Site
cards.title: Tour Taft’s boyhood home
cards.subtitle: 2038 Auburn Avenue, Cincinnati
cards.notes: Start at the Taft Education Center, watch the orientation film, and ask a ranger about the next house tour.
cards.short_summary: A nearby National Park Service historic site with self-guided rooms and ranger tours.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service says there are no entrance fees at William Howard Taft National Historic Site or its visitor center.
cards.source_title: Fees & Passes | William Howard Taft National Historic Site
cards.access_notes: Check current operating hours; the NPS says house tours and facility access can vary by day and holiday.

cards.title: Walk Burnet Woods trails
cards.subtitle: Burnet Woods Park, adjoining UC
cards.notes: Take the open marked trails around the woods and lake; obey posted closures, including the closed lower Bard Owl Trail section.
cards.short_summary: A close-to-campus walk through a 90-acre city park with trails and a fishing lake.
cards.evidence_claim: Cincinnati Parks identifies Burnet Woods as adjoining UC with hiking trails, and states Cincinnati Parks are free for all to use.
cards.source_title: Burnet Woods & Trailside Nature Center | Cincinnati Parks
cards.access_notes: Park hours are listed as 6 a.m.–10 p.m.; follow closures and posted safety notices.

cards.title: Meet by Mirror Lake
cards.subtitle: Eden Park
cards.notes: Use the paved walkways to reach Mirror Lake, then circle the Bettman Fountain and Spring House Gazebo for an easy outdoor catch-up.
cards.short_summary: A named Eden Park landmark with paths, gardens, and nearby seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Cincinnati Parks lists Mirror Lake and the Bettman Fountain among Eden Park features and states Cincinnati Parks are free for all to use.
cards.access_notes: Eden Park is listed as open daily from 6 a.m.–10 p.m.; the lake area is outdoors and unreserved.

cards.title: Walk the Barr Labyrinth
cards.subtitle: Smale Riverfront Park, downtown Cincinnati
cards.notes: Follow the labyrinth’s path at your own pace, then continue along the riverfront on the park’s paved public spaces.
cards.short_summary: A named walkable feature in the downtown riverfront park.
cards.evidence_claim: Cincinnati Parks lists Barr Labyrinth as a Smale Riverfront Park feature and states Cincinnati Parks are free for all to use.
cards.access_notes: The park lists hours of 6 a.m.–11 p.m.; visitors 17 and younger need a parent or guardian after 9 p.m.

cards.title: Spread out on the Civic Lawn
cards.subtitle: Washington Park, Over-the-Rhine
cards.notes: Bring a book or a conversation to the Civic Lawn, then use the park’s paved paths and free Wi‑Fi without buying anything.
cards.short_summary: A public lawn and gathering space in Washington Park.
cards.evidence_claim: Cincinnati Parks lists the Civic Lawn and free Wi‑Fi at Washington Park and states Cincinnati Parks are free for all to use.
cards.access_notes: The park lists hours of 6 a.m.–11 p.m.; visitors 17 and younger need a parent or guardian after 9 p.m.

cards.title: Walk to the Bellevue overlook
cards.subtitle: Clifton Heights
cards.notes: Use the paved walking path and pause at the overlook for downtown and Ohio River views, keeping to the maintained park areas.
cards.short_summary: A nearby Clifton Heights park with a paved path and city-and-river viewpoint.
cards.evidence_claim: Cincinnati Parks describes Bellevue Hill Park as having a paved walking path and views of downtown Cincinnati and the Ohio River; Cincinnati Parks are free for all to use.
cards.access_notes: Use the public walking path and follow posted park rules; no reservation or purchase is needed for ordinary park use.
